$comment: Content metadata owned by the content steward, not by developers.
Each entry becomes Azure Blob metadata at upload time, and the blob indexer
maps blob metadata into index fields of the same name automatically.
'folder' selects which language container path the file is uploaded to, and
therefore which per-language index and analyzer it lands in. One index per
language exists because the Azure AI Search analyzer property is set on a
field at index creation time, so there is no per-document analyzer.
'translation_status' is the human assurance behind the text and is what the
knowledge:translation_gate key selects on. Ordered strongest first:
source     authored in this language, not derived from anything
certified  translated and formally certified
reviewed   translated and reviewed in market
machine    machine translated, unreviewed
Moving a document from reviewed to certified is a metadata change, and
changing which levels a market accepts is a configuration change. Neither
is a code change.
'source_document' and 'source_version' are what make translation drift
detectable. A derived document records the version of the source it was
made from. When the source moves on, the derived document stays approved
and becomes quietly stale, which nothing else in the system would reveal.
IsDeleted is the soft-delete marker. The indexer's deletion detection policy
watches it, and it must exist from the very first indexer run.
